items.locator: Warnings and Precautions §5.3 Psychiatric Disorders: depression, mood disturbance, psychosis, suicidality and aggressive behavior are reported; patients developing depression or mood disturbance should stop isotretinoin and promptly contact the prescriber, with further evaluation as needed.
items.version: DailyMed isotretinoin prescribing information revised July 2026; currentness live-rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.stem: A client taking isotretinoin reports new depressive symptoms and a marked mood change. Which instruction is most appropriate?

options.A: Continue isotretinoin and discuss the symptoms at the next routine visit.
options.B: Stop isotretinoin and promptly contact the prescriber for evaluation.
options.C: Double the next isotretinoin dose if the mood symptoms improve.
options.D: Assume the symptoms are unrelated to isotretinoin unless psychosis develops.

items.rationale: Current isotretinoin labeling warns about depression and other psychiatric disorders and instructs patients who develop depression or mood disturbance to stop the drug and promptly contact the prescriber. Option B is correct. A and D delay evaluation, and C is unsafe and unsupported.
items.finding: Fresh audit removed padded wording and retained the current July 2026 label instruction.

items.source_name: CDC/NIOSH — Control of Smoke From Laser/Electric Surgical Procedures
items.locator: NIOSH Hazard Controls HC11: surgical smoke can contain toxic gases, vapors, bioaerosols and cellular material; local exhaust ventilation/smoke evacuation should capture smoke close to its source and remain active whenever airborne particles are produced.
items.version: DHHS (NIOSH) Publication 96-128; page last reviewed 2014 and recommendation remains referenced by current NIOSH surgical-smoke guidance; live currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.stem: During electrosurgery, why should local surgical-smoke evacuation remain active whenever smoke is produced?

options.B: To shorten the duration of surgery.
options.C: To capture hazardous airborne contaminants close to their source.
options.D: To prevent electrical interference with monitoring equipment.

items.rationale: NIOSH recommends local exhaust control because surgical smoke can contain hazardous gases, vapors, particles, bioaerosols, and cellular material. Option C states the infection/occupational-safety purpose. The other choices are not the function of surgical-smoke evacuation.
items.finding: Fresh audit removed artificial option padding and verified that the older NIOSH hazard-control document remains an active referenced recommendation rather than treating its publication year as evidence of obsolescence.

items.source_name: OSHA — Hospitals eTool: Surgical Suite, Laser Hazards
items.locator: Laser eye-protection guidance and 29 CFR 1926.102(c)(2): protective eyewear must be suitable for the specific laser wavelength and provide adequate optical density; eyewear is marked with wavelength and optical density.
items.stem: During a surgical laser procedure, which eye protection is appropriate for personnel exposed to the laser hazard?

options.B: Standard splash goggles regardless of wavelength.
options.C: Laser eyewear rated for the specific wavelength and required optical density.
options.D: No eye protection for staff who are not operating the laser.

items.rationale: Laser protective eyewear must match the wavelength and provide adequate optical density for the hazard. Option C is correct. Ordinary sunglasses and splash goggles are not substitutes, and reflected or scattered laser energy can endanger personnel other than the operator.
items.finding: Fresh audit replaced verbose alternatives with parallel, directly testable PPE choices.

items.source_name: U.S. FDA — MRI Benefits and Risks
items.locator: MRI safety screening: carefully screen people and objects entering the MR environment; implanted devices must be positively identified as MR Safe or MR Conditional under the specified conditions; unknown status should not be assumed safe.
items.version: Current FDA MRI safety guidance live-rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.stem: Before an MRI examination, which action is essential?

options.A: Screen the client and all items for MR hazards and verify the MR status of implanted devices.
options.B: Skip implant screening if the client previously had an MRI.
options.C: Leave small metallic objects in place because only large objects are hazardous.
options.D: Assume an unknown implant is safe unless symptoms develop during scanning.

items.rationale: FDA guidance emphasizes screening people and objects for MRI hazards and verifying the MR safety status of implants before scanning. Option A is correct. Prior MRI exposure does not automatically establish present-device safety, small ferromagnetic objects can be hazardous, and an unknown implant should not be assumed safe.
items.finding: Fresh audit removed the irrelevant anxiety cue from the stem and made the tested MRI-safety decision direct.

items.source_name: CDC — Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices for Safe Healthcare Delivery in All Settings
items.locator: Performance Monitoring and Feedback: identify and monitor adherence to infection-prevention practices, use standardized tools when available, and provide prompt, regular feedback on adherence and related outcomes.
items.stem: A hospital audits hand-hygiene opportunities and completed actions, then reports the results to staff. What is the primary purpose?

options.B: To create a discipline-only ranking of individual staff.
options.C: To monitor adherence, identify gaps, and support improvement through feedback.
options.D: To collect data without changing practice.

items.rationale: CDC recommends monitoring adherence to infection-prevention practices and providing prompt, regular feedback so gaps and outcomes can be improved. Option C is correct. Monitoring is not intended to replace education, function only as punishment, or remain disconnected from improvement.
items.finding: Fresh audit simplified choices and aligned the item directly with CDC's Performance Monitoring and Feedback section.

items.source_name: CDC/NIOSH — Conserving Personal Protective Equipment During Supply Shortages
items.locator: Crisis-capacity strategies section: crisis measures are used temporarily during known shortages when conventional and contingency capacity cannot meet demand; they carry higher risk and should be discontinued as supply conditions improve.
items.stem: Which statement best describes crisis-capacity PPE strategies during a severe shortage?

options.A: They are preferred routine practice even after supplies recover.
options.B: They make required PPE unnecessary for direct care.
options.C: They apply only to nonclinical staff.
options.D: They are temporary shortage measures used when conventional and contingency strategies cannot meet demand.

items.rationale: CDC/NIOSH distinguishes conventional, contingency, and crisis capacity. Crisis strategies are temporary measures for severe shortages and are not a substitute for routine practice once supply improves. Option D is correct; A, B, and C misstate their purpose and scope.
items.finding: Fresh audit removed lengthy absolute distractors while preserving clinically meaningful distinctions among PPE-capacity strategies.

items.source_name: HHS CHEMM — START Adult Triage Algorithm
items.locator: START Adult Triage Algorithm: Red = Immediate; the person can be helped by immediate intervention/transport and needs medical attention within minutes for survival, including airway, breathing, or circulation compromise.
items.version: HHS CHEMM current web publication of the Benson-modified START algorithm; CHEMM background identifies the 1996 modification; page/version currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN 2026 prioritization/Management of Care check completed first.
items.stem: During START mass-casualty triage, what does a red tag indicate?

options.A: Immediate — treatment and transport are time-critical for survival.
options.C: Delayed — serious injury without immediate life threat.
options.D: Expectant/deceased — immediate resources are not directed first.

items.rationale: In the HHS CHEMM START algorithm, red means Immediate: the person needs time-critical intervention and transport to survive. Green is minor, yellow is delayed, and black is expectant/deceased. Option A is correct.
items.finding: Fresh audit treated the item as prioritization, verified NCSBN 2026 first, documented the published START variant, and removed explanatory padding.

items.locator: Contact Precautions: use gown and gloves for interactions that may involve contact with the patient or the patient's environment, in addition to Standard Precautions and task-specific PPE.
items.version: CDC Transmission-Based Precautions page current; live-rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.stem: A client is on Contact Precautions. Which PPE is required for interactions that may involve contact with the client or environment?

options.D: No PPE if hand hygiene is performed.

items.rationale: CDC Contact Precautions call for gown and gloves for interactions involving the patient or patient environment. Additional PPE may be required under Standard Precautions for specific tasks. Option C is correct; the other choices omit the core contact barriers.
items.finding: Fresh audit reduced the options to clean PPE alternatives without embedding rationales in each choice.

items.source_name: CDC — Isolation Precautions Glossary / Airborne Infection Isolation Room
items.locator: Airborne Infection Isolation Room (AIIR): a single-occupancy room with monitored negative pressure relative to surrounding areas; AIIR placement is recommended for patients requiring Airborne Precautions.
items.stem: Which room is preferred for a hospitalized client who requires Airborne Precautions?

options.A: An airborne infection isolation room with negative pressure relative to adjacent areas.
options.C: A semiprivate room with ordinary ventilation.
options.D: Any private room without pressure control.

items.rationale: An AIIR is maintained at negative pressure relative to adjacent areas so air flows into the room rather than outward. It is the preferred inpatient placement for Airborne Precautions. Option A is correct. Positive-pressure rooms serve a different purpose, and ordinary private or semiprivate rooms do not provide equivalent engineering control.
items.finding: Fresh audit removed option padding and focused the item on the defining engineering control.

items.locator: Management of Care — Legal Rights and Responsibilities/Assignment and Delegation activity statements: provide care within legal scope, recognize limitations of self and others and use resources, consider client acuity and staff competence when making assignments.
items.version: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness live-rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.stem: A medical-surgical RN is floated to a pediatric ICU where the nurse has not previously practiced. Which assignment is safest?

options.A: The unit's most unstable child because an active RN license establishes specialty competence.
options.B: A full independent PICU assignment with no unit support.
options.C: Any assignment needed for staffing, regardless of the nurse's verified competencies.
options.D: An assignment matched to verified skills, with orientation, supervision, or workload modification as needed.

items.rationale: NCSBN expects nurses to recognize professional limitations, use appropriate resources, practice within legal scope, and consider competence in assignments. Option D protects clients while allowing appropriate support and orientation. Licensure alone does not establish competence for every specialty assignment, so A, B, and C are unsafe.
items.finding: Fresh audit replaced a secondary professional-source rationale with the mandatory primary NCSBN source because the item tests scope, assignment, and competence.
